column1: # BASELINE of EXPOSED EXACT-COUNT sites -- r7241+70.1 (node 70), on 60's detector (S10, r7240/r7242).  Data, not code.
# ** A RECORD OF ADJUDICATIONS, NOT A LIST OF EXEMPTIONS ** -- the same rule as the pin baselines.
#   One line per key:  receipt <TAB> comparison (source text, whitespace collapsed) <TAB> verdict <TAB> what was read
# Verdicts: DELIBERATE (the exact count is the claim, and its control is in the receipt), FALSE-POSITIVE (the
# detector's taint reaches a set nobody else moves), SCOPED (the counted set is already this seat's own),
# UNADJUDICATED (counted, not yet read -- the ceiling in check_exact_counts.py may only fall).
# The 24 UNADJUDICATED at r7241+70.1 are all in receipts outside 60's two directories, which no sweep had reached.
# Seventeen of them are `== 0` over paper prose or a document -- an ABSENCE asserted as an exact count, which any
# seat's legitimate use of the word turns red; noted per row so the reading can start there.

r7246 (60).  The FOUR is the claim -- four papers at the top of in-degree -- and the companion assertion on the same gate ties it to the graph's own size (`_maxdeg == len(g) - 1`), so a grown corpus fails loudly here instead of drifting silently.  Read: the gate and its in-degree computation.  A paper added at top in-degree SHOULD fire this.

r7246 (60).  ABSENCE GUARD: the zero is the claim -- no gate has an origin that no longer exists -- and the receipt carries a POSITIVE control, asserting non-zero counts over the same population elsewhere.  Read at r7246 as one of the thirty.  No ceiling can replace it: `<= 0` and `== 0` are the same predicate.

r7246 (60).  ABSENCE GUARD with a positive control in the same receipt: the zero says no receipt still uses the open-form-only lookup, and reintroducing one SHOULD fire it.  Read at r7246 as one of the thirty.

r7246 (60).  *** THE ONE GENUINE SITE of the thirty this revision read: an exact NON-ZERO count of the receipts carrying the strike-tolerant lookup, over a population any seat grows by adding a receipt. ***  The prescribed repair is `>= 13`, and this receipt is not this seat's to edit, so the repair is ROUTED rather than applied and the verdict says so.  Read: the gate, its two populations and the thirteen it names.

r7246 (60).  ABSENCE GUARD over another receipt's code, with a positive control in the same receipt.  The zero says no `'HEAD'` literal remains in B1, and one reappearing SHOULD fire it.  Read at r7246 as one of the thirty.  D1 is on this seat's do-not-edit list, so nothing here is applied to it.

r7246 (60).  The counted set is read at a PINNED commit -- the gate's own `BEFORE` -- so nobody moves it and the detector's taint reaching it is the false positive the verdict names.  Read: the gate, its `BEFORE` binding and the rows it counts there.

r7246 (60).  Same shape and same reason: the two rows are counted at the pinned `BEFORE` state, which no seat can move.  The detector cannot see a pin passed through a helper, which is the limit S10's honest bound declares.

r7246 (60).  ABSENCE GUARD, and the receipt's own sentence is its control: `the probe's arithmetic was CORRECT: 0 of N appear verbatim -- the object was wrong, not the count`, with the denominator printed beside the zero.  A sentence appearing verbatim later SHOULD fire it.

r7246 (60).  The THREE is the claim -- class (ii) is three, in one paper -- and the receipt already reasoned about growth: it PRINTS the paper count as reported rather than asserting it, saying `the corpus may gain one`.  A new paper carrying an overclaimed sigma SHOULD fire this gate, which is what it is for.
r7246 (60).  The companion half of the same claim and its control: the per-paper three must also be the corpus-wide three, so a hit in any other paper breaks the pair rather than slipping past it.

r7246 (60).  The counted set is the baseline rows carrying THIS SEAT'S OWN STAMP from a completed pass -- no other seat writes that stamp -- so the set is already this seat's own, which is what SCOPED names.  Read: the STAMP binding and the MINE filter above the gate.

r7246 (60).  The two are the figure rows this revision itself corrected, selected by its own stamp -- its own work, counted.  Read: the _FIG filter and the gate's account of the two readings it repaired.

r7246 (60).  The split IS the claim -- three of the twenty-four are this seat's and twenty-one are other seats' -- and it is computed from the paths rather than asserted.  If the OPEN subclass grows the reading is stale and the gate SHOULD fire; that is the behaviour wanted, not a defect.
r7246 (60).  The other half of the same split, same reading: a grown subclass makes the routing stale and firing is the point.

r7246 (60).  The seven are the readings with a computable ground, enumerated in the gate's own prose as five named kinds; the count is the claim and the enumeration is its control.  A new reading without a ground SHOULD fire it -- the gate's sentence says an exemption wearing a verdict's clothes is what it exists to catch.

r7246 (60).  ABSENCE GUARD: the zero is this seat's share of the unread-figure backlog, and its purpose is to fire if any of this seat's sites RETURNS to the backlog.  Its companion exact count on the whole backlog was an exact count on a set other seats lower, and r7246 repaired that one to `<=` rather than adjudicating it.

r7246 (60).  THE EXEMPLAR OF THE CLASS: an absence over the paper bodies whose POSITIVE CONTROL is stated on the line above in so many words -- `assert len(live) > 0 ... an absence over no files at all would be vacuous`.  This is what every absence guard should look like, and r7246 found five that do not.

r7246 (60).  ABSENCE GUARD with historical controls on the same gate: the live population is zero because the row it audited was CLOSED, and the companion assertions count the pre-closure populations as non-zero.  A reopened row SHOULD fire it.

r7246 (60).  The sixty is the claim about THIS SWEEP, and the receipt names the additions since by commit -- the eightieth and eighty-first are named with their revisions in the gate's own prose.  So a further addition fires the gate and is then named in the same place, which is the handling the corpus wants rather than a ceiling.
